Thanks again for the call today — really appreciate the time. Quick recap and a few asks so we can put together a formal pricing package and an SOW for your procurement team.

Recap from our discovery:
- Workload: real-time payment assistant + batch data enrichment for transaction history.
- Estimated tokens: 6–7M tokens/day in early usage (approx 180–210M/month), with a target growth path to ~12–15M/day (~360–450M/month) in year 2.
- Required privacy posture: Private VPC deployment, customer-managed VPC with Redwood control plane.
- Environments: prod + staging + dev (you mentioned potentially an additional analytics environment).

Open items / asks for pricing: 
1) Can you confirm the expected baseline monthly token range we should price for (pick one): 150–250M / 250–400M / 400M+?
2) Do you have a target blended $/1M tokens or a monthly budget range for inference (ballpark is fine)?
3) Final confirmation on environment count (prod, staging, dev, analytics?) and whether each environment needs reserved capacity or can share capacity.
4) Procurement contact and timeline for reviewing a draft MSA + SOW.

What I'll put together after your reply: two pricing options (Reserved commitment + license per environment vs. Enterprise license with per-environment add-ons), plus the SKU-level unit economics showing $/1M tokens at different commit levels. I’ll also include our support tiers (Standard vs. Premium) and the impact on overall unit economics.

Next steps: if it works for you I can send a draft pricing sheet and a short example SOW by tomorrow. If helpful we can also schedule a 30-min follow-up with our Solutions Engineer (Marissa) to run through capacity planning.

Thanks,
Ben

Thanks Aisha — great, that gives us everything we need to build a clean proposal. Attached are three artifacts for review:
- Redwood_Pricing_Sheet_paymentsai_v2.pdf (pricing options + unit economics)
- Master_Services_Agreement_draft.docx (redlines welcome)
- security_evidence_SOC2_summary.pdf (SOC 2 summary + logs and audit cadence)

High-level pricing summary (baseline 150–250M/mo):
1) Option A — Reserved commit + per-environment license
   - Reserved commit: tiered pricing tied to committed monthly tokens. Example:
     * 150M/month commit: ~$72,000/month total -> implied ~$480 / 1M tokens (includes reserved infra + runtime optimizations and prefix caching assumptions)
     * 250M/month commit: ~$110,000/month total -> implied ~$440 / 1M tokens
   - Per-environment license: $5,000/month per non-prod environment, $12,500/month for prod environment (includes orchestration, admin console, and audit logging).
   - Support tiers: Standard (included) — 24x5 ticketing, 8-hour response for Sev1; Premium (+20% uplift) — 24x7 on-call, 2-hour response for Sev1, quarterly on-site/remote reviews and runbooks.

2) Option B — Enterprise license (flat platform fee) + usage overage pricing
   - Platform fee: $65,000/month (covers up to 150M tokens/month).
   - Overage: $420 / 1M tokens over the included commit.
   - Per-environment: included up to 3 environments; additional environment: $4,000/month.
   - Support tiers: Premium available as an add-on (+15% on platform fee) with guaranteed SLOs and named technical lead.

Unit economics example (baseline 200M/month):
- Option A blended: ~$88k/month -> implied ~$440 / 1M tokens (includes license + reserved infra + standard support).
- Option B blended: platform fee + small overage similarly lands in the ~$420–$470 / 1M tokens band depending on environment count and support.

Notes and assumptions:
- These are order-of-magnitude examples. Final pricing will be refined based on final token distribution (seq length / prompt vs. response split), steady-state cache hit rates, and whether you require dedicated physical isolation (on-prem) vs managed VPC.
- The per-environment license is meant to cover admin/observability features and audit access; environments that share capacity and don't need separate control-plane features can be discounted.
